dispositions.topic_text: The deployment mechanism, hostname, certificate, and routing that ensure an exclusive host-only owner-interface cookie scope
dispositions.what: As State 2 round-120 T28 and round-121 T2: the owner interface's own host name, its certificate and routing (TLS at the route, a VPN-resolved name, or a gateway virtual host forwarding only to the owner interface), chosen by the Factory's platform deployment; every option keeps A13 rule 1: no other HTTPS service of the host answers under that name or receives the owner session cookie (decided under the owner's direction of 2026-11-24, matrix P6).
keeps:
the deployment gives the owner interface a host name of its
   own, under which no other HTTPS service answers
options: Allocate a dedicated DNS host name and certificate terminating directly at the owner-interface route.
Allocate a dedicated internal or VPN-resolved host name and certificate reachable only through the owner's VPN.
Use a gateway with a dedicated host name whose virtual host forwards only to the owner interface.
consequences: A public or private DNS name needs lifecycle and certificate management but gives straightforward host isolation.
An internal or VPN name narrows reachability but requires every owner device to resolve and trust it.
A gateway centralizes TLS but must ensure no other service is routed under that host name.
